errors.description: The frame runs down to mid-thigh, so the pocket opening occupies roughly a third of the frame rather than the 40-80% dominance target; a band of plain leg cloth carries no information.
errors.actual: Opening spans about 36% of frame width in the upper-left; lower half of frame is plain leg.
errors.correction: Bottom edge could sit roughly a hand's width below the horizontal run of the pocket opening instead of at mid-thigh. The rounded corner is still fully sharp and unmistakable at this scale.

errors.description: The besom pocket drawn on the opposite hip is reproduced at nearly the same visual weight as the subject, so it mildly competes for attention.
errors.expected: Besom present as in the drawing but clearly secondary.
errors.actual: Besom rendered crisply and roughly level with the subject pocket.
errors.correction: Faithful to the blueprint (the besom IS in the drawing); could be softened by depth of field. Not a geometry error.

notes: Illustration shows a trouser three-quarter front: waistband with belt loops, a red-outlined J-shaped opening on the near hip (short vertical drop off the waistband, rounded corner, long horizontal run inboard toward the crease), and a plain besom on the far hip. The candidate reproduces that geometry closely: the scoop opening starts under a belt loop at the waistband, drops, turns through a smooth round corner and runs horizontally to the crease, terminating at the same landmark as the drawing. The corner is genuinely ROUND, which is the distinguishing feature against the square/diamond/arc siblings. The besom on the opposite hip is present, matching the drawing. No red leaked into the cloth — the whole garment is charcoal wool; no annotations, numbers or leader lines anywhere. Two minor findings, both composition/emphasis, no geometry defects.
